projectDescription: Live stock view, exception queue and per-location drilldown on top of the Phase 2 sync
overview: Phase 2 put a nightly two-way sync between the point-of-sale and the warehouse system, with a reconciliation report and alerting on failed runs. The sync is running and the weekly by-hand reconciliation is gone. What is left is visibility: the data is correct now, but reading it still means opening two systems and a report attachment.
overviewExtra: Phase 3 is the read layer. One place that answers what is in stock right now, which lines disagreed and need a human, and how each location is tracking. No new integrations, no changes to the sync itself.

services.description: On-hand by SKU across all three locations, sourced from the Phase 2 sync, refreshed on each run.
By SKU, description, location and stock band, so a question about one line takes seconds rather than an export.
Every line where the two systems did not reconcile on the last run, oldest first, with both values shown side by side.
Mark a line resolved with a short note. The note stays on the line so the next person sees why it was closed.
A line unresolved past a threshold is surfaced at the top. Exceptions that nobody looks at are the failure mode this is built against.
The same stock and exception views scoped to one store, for the people who only run one.
Exception count and unreconciled value per location over time, so a store that is drifting shows up before it becomes a stock-out.

lineItems.description: Phase 3: Ops dashboard, build and handover

investment.note: All amounts are in US Dollars. Phases 1 and 2 are complete and invoiced separately.

whatThisCovers: Build, test and deploy of the three views described above.
Access for named users, with the roles you already use in the warehouse system.
A handover session and a written runbook covering the exception workflow.
Two weeks of post-handover support for defects in what was delivered.
additionalWork: Anything outside the three views above is quoted separately before it is started. That includes new integrations, changes to the Phase 2 sync logic, historical backfill beyond what the sync already holds, and any reporting that leaves the dashboard, for example scheduled email or a data export feed.
termsAndConditions: Fixed price. The price does not move unless the scope above changes, and a scope change is agreed in writing before any work on it starts.
Timelines are confirmed at kick-off, once access to the reporting environment is in place.
Access required: read access to the Phase 2 sync database and to the warehouse system's user roles.
Work delivered under this proposal is owned by Acme Retail on final payment.

customSections.heading: DEFINITION OF DONE
content: The live stock view shows the same on-hand figure as the warehouse system for a sampled set of 50 SKUs across all three locations.
Every line that failed to reconcile on the most recent sync run appears in the exception queue, and a resolved line leaves the queue with its note attached.
A named user at a single location can reach their own store's view and cannot see another store's drilldown.
The runbook has been walked through once with the ops lead, on the live system, without Sam driving.
